The co-pilot has to determine the take-off parameters based on the weight of the plane (that's what the tablet to the right is for) to optimize fuel burn. Some newer super-liners can weight themselves both at the gate and in-flight.

The co-pilot also sets the take-off thrust (pilot pushes up throttle to launch; says "cross-check," and the the co-pilot adjusts it to what they need so the pilot can focus on the takeoff). A lot of post take-off/in-flight is totally automated. Once they clear the runway, waypoints, climb/descent rates, etc. can all be adjusted by turning dials on the auto-navigation.
